subtopic: Long context serving / KV bandwidth and capacity
learningObjective: Reason about the primary bottlenecks that appear when scaling LLM inference to very long contexts.
stem: Select all statements that correctly characterize challenges specific to long-context (say 32K+ token) LLM serving. (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: Per-token KV cache grows linearly with context length; at fixed HBM budget, doubling context length approximately halves the maximum concurrent batch size, directly cutting throughput.
TPOT is independent of context length because decode still processes only one new token per step; the KV cache size is a memory-only concern with no effect on per-step latency.

Decode-step attention time grows linearly with context length because the attention kernel reads the full growing KV cache each step; at long context, attention read bandwidth can rival weight read bandwidth per step, changing the per-step latency composition.
Long context has no impact on prefill latency: prefill is a single forward pass that always takes the same wall-clock time regardless of prompt length, so TTFT stays constant with longer prompts.

explanation: A is correct: KV grows linearly with context, capping batch size. C is correct: attention read cost per decode step grows linearly with context (whole KV read), and at long context attention bytes can rival weight bytes, increasing TPOT. B is wrong: TPOT does grow with context because attention reads scale linearly. D is wrong: prefill time is roughly proportional to P (or P^2/M in the FlashAttention regime for attention); longer prompts increase TTFT.

optionExplanations.D: Wrong: prefill scales with prompt length.

assumptions: 'Long context' means the KV cache is a significant fraction of HBM.
Attention kernel reads the full KV each decode step (no sliding window or sparse attention).
nonImplications: Does not imply sliding-window or approximate attention cannot help; they are exactly the mitigations.
Does not imply KV quantization is quality-neutral.
